newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA TELECOM CO BATTLES FINANCIAL CRISIS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA TELECOM CO BATTLES FINANCIAL CRISIS.

text.p: Bulgarian Telecommunications Company (BTC), which is preparing for privatisation, will struggle to meet its debt payments to international lenders this year, its new chairman said on Thursday.
Marian Dragostinov, who was appointed this week, said the new management had inherited financial chaos.

"If the new tariffs had not been approved by the cabinet today, the BTC could have the rare chance to be included in the Guinness Book of World Records and become the first bankrupt telecom company in the world," he told a news conference.

The BTC has been granted loans worth $150 million for the modernisation of the telephone system from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, the European Investment Bank and the World Bank.
The BTC is due to start payments of the principal and interest rates of the loans in the second half of this year.
Dragostinov gave no details of the sums involved but said all measures would be taken to make the payments and representatives of the banks will come to Sofia for talks in early March.

"With the new tariffs which will be smoothly regulated based on macroeconomic parameters and through introducing new sources for gaining funds, which will be not traditional, I am 99 percent sure that we will be able to meet our payments to the creditors," Dragostinov told Reuters.
The interim cabinet approved on Thursday a 525 percent increase of telephone charges from March 1.

It has also approved the introduction of a scheme of monthly revisions of the tariffs, mainly according to the lev/dollar exchange rate and the inflation rate, said the new Posts and Communications Committee chairman Antoni Slavinski.
The BTC owes $25 million to foreign operators and its uncollected payments are 5.4 billion levs, Dragostinov said.
